definitions.explanation: A category or class of people or things grouped by shared characteristics. Often used in the pattern ～の部類に入る to say something belongs to a certain category.

examples.japanese: それは{高|たか}い{部類|ぶるい}に{入|はい}る。
examples.english: That falls into the expensive category.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{背|せ}が{高|たか}い{部類|ぶるい}だ。
examples.english: He is in the tall category.

examples.japanese: この{店|みせ}のラーメンは{全国的|ぜんこくてき}に{見|み}ても{美味|おい}しい{部類|ぶるい}に{入|はい}ると{思|おも}う。
examples.english: I think this shop's ramen ranks among the tasty ones even on a national level.

notes:
Most commonly appears in the pattern ～の{部類|ぶるい}に{入|はい}る (to fall into the category of ~). Used to classify something relative to others of its kind.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～の{部類|ぶるい}に{入|はい}る (to belong to the ~ category)
- ～{部類|ぶるい}だ (is in the ~ group)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {上|うえ}の{部類|ぶるい} (the upper category)
- {珍|めずら}しい{部類|ぶるい} (the rare category)
- {優秀|ゆうしゅう}な{部類|ぶるい} (the excellent category)
